papers.title: A high-dimensional population code in the bat motor cortex during natural dexterous flight
papers.abstract_snippet: Bats use their hand-like wings to reproduce natural flights with wingbeat-level precision. Rather than mainly tracking the wingbeat cycle, the wing motor cortex generates sparse, distinct population states with little shared variance across wingbeats, resulting in a high-dimensional code distinct from that typically observed in constrained tasks.
